newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's reserves up to $4.05 billion in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's reserves up to $4.05 billion in 1996.

text.p: Morocco's foreign reserves rose 3.0 billion dirhams to 36.5 billion dirhams ($4.05 billion) in 1996, or the equivalent of six months' imports, the governor of Bank al-Maghrib, (central bank) Mohamed Seqat said on Tuesday.
Seqat told the national council of money and saving Morocco's foreign reserves have improved due to the current account deficit drop in 1996.
"Our foreign reserves rose by 3.0 billion dirhams to 36.5 billion dirhams or the equivalent of six months' imports compared with 5.5 months' imports in 1995," Seqat said.
Earlier, the Finance Minister Mohamed Kabbaj said the current account deficit was cut to 1.2 percent in 1996 from 4.6 percent in 1995.

In a forecast on the development of the Moroccan economy in 1997, the central bank governor said: "On the basis of the figures we have, the money supply would not exceed 6.0 to 7.0 percent for the whole year of 1997."
Seqat said this target takes into account the increase of the non-agricultural gross domestic product of 3.0 percent."
"It also aims to contain the price hike at the level of 1996 and avoid the aggravation of the current account," the governor said.
According to the official figures, the inflation was lowered to 3.0 percent in 1996, from 6.1 percent in 1995.
Officials forecast a growth of 3.0 to 4.0 percent in Morocco's GDP in 1997 against 11.8 percent in 1996.
